name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield 5.16% and 30-year 5.62% on 6 Nov, after the Bank of England's rate rise
state: The 10-year gilt yield closed at 5.16% on 6 Nov, 28bp lower than a month earlier but 69bp higher on the year, and the 30-year yield was 5.62% (Trading Economics). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise in more than three years. No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported; Watch is kept while yields stay near multi-year highs.
for_you: Gilt yields feed into fixed mortgage rates and annuity pricing; lenders tend to reprice within weeks.
why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
